newsitem.title: UK: London Freight - The Pacific is weaker.
newsitem.headline: London Freight - The Pacific is weaker.

text.p: Most market observers considered that the freight market was continuing to drift lower, although not all reported fixtures fitted this scenario

There was little doubt that conditions for Capers and Panamaxes continued to weaken in the Pacific but there were a few Panamax fixtures concluded in the Atlantic that defied the trend. However, brokers reported tonnage building up in certain key loading areas without underlying depth of inquiry to sustain current levels. The BFI fell again, down 12 points to 1481, and the Baltic Handy Index lost five to 1102.

Grain brokers were surprised at the firm rates obtained by the 1974-built Cornilios for a prompt parcel of about 48,250 grains 54' Paranagua/Continent, reported at close to $18.50 paid by Graincoop, and by the 1975-built Aghios Minas 64,040 dwt delivery retro passing Passero 23 March for an E Coast S America round, reported at $10,000 daily paid by Saroc. It was said that a number of early unfixed Panamaxes were still available in the Plate/Brazil area including Afros 75,426 dwt, Amadeus 66,916 dwt and Georgia 63,308 dwt. Delays in loading at Paranagua, quoted at up to 35/40 days, have severely reduced topoff business.

Charterers have instead turned to fixing Handy-Sizes from the Plate direct to destination instead of completing with 10,000 or 15,000 tonnes from Paranagua. Some brokers now think Handy-Size rates are beginning to decline slightly from S America. In the Mississippi the problems caused by the stranded chermtrans Belocean at South West Pass were reported to have eased to the extent of 35' draft being permissible in the river. There were unsubstantiated reports that S Koreans had fixed 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for spot loading at a lower $24.00 no combo (possibly involving Sumava), and that Continental were firm at this level for April against tonnage indicating $25.50 combo. There were rumours of Cargill booking Evangelos CH for 25,000 wheat St Lawrence/Venezuela at $23.50.

British Steel were understood to have booked a Caper for Hampton Roads/Redcar, and Cape Cathay 149,000 dwt open UK early May was fixed to Al Jubail, both on private terms. Deiulemar were said to have fixed Golden Cape for 110,000 coal Hampton Roads/Constanza for end April at $7.25 although some thought this business was old. SCF Vladimir 54,000 was fixed on private terms in the Atlantic for phosphate. Another weaker Panamax coal fixture was reported in the Far East where Navix booked Northern Princess 71,000 dwt on subjects delivery Taiwan 10 April for a trip via E Australia to Japan at $12,350 daily.

The geared ICL Vikraman 55,879 dwt was rumoured taken by Pan Ocean delivery Continent trip Far East, and Hercegovina 30,880 dwt was linked with Fednav for a Lakes round, but full details were lacking. In the East Clipp fixed Calliroe Patronicola 29,000 dwt delivery W Australia 11/18 April for a trip with Alumina to Singapore-Japan range at $8,000 daily plus $90,000 bonus.
